Most people guess their sprinkler run times. A catch-cup test measures what each zone actually puts down, in about 20 minutes, with a few cups and a ruler.

**How to do it:** set out 8–12 identical straight-sided containers (tuna cans or plastic cups) in a grid across one zone, away from the heads themselves. Run the zone for 10–20 minutes. Measure the water depth in each container with a ruler and enter them below.

      { k: 'need', l: 'Water needed per week, including rain', t: 'wdep', d: (u, v) => { const n = NEED[(v && v.pre) || 'peak'] || NEED.peak; return u === 'us' ? n[0] : n[1]; }, w: 3, h: 'Subtract any rain that fell that week.' },
      { k: 'days', l: 'Watering days per week', t: 'select', d: '3', opts: [['1', '1'], ['2', '2'], ['3', '3'], ['4', '4']], w: 3 }
    ],
    onChange(k, api) { if (k === 'pre' && NEED[api.get('pre')]) api.setDisp('need', NEED[api.get('pre')][api.units() === 'us' ? 0 : 1]); if (k === 'need') api.setChoice('pre', 'custom'); },
    compute(v, U) {
      const c = (v.cups || []).filter(x => x >= 0);
      if (!(v.min > 0) || c.length < 2) return U.empty('Enter the run time and at least two cup readings (eight or more is better).');
      const n = c.length, avg = c.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / n;
      if (!(avg > 0)) return U.empty('All the cups are empty: check the zone ran.');
      const s = c.slice().sort((a, b) => a - b), q = Math.max(1, Math.round(n / 4)), lq = s.slice(0, q).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / q;
      const rate = avg / (v.min / 60), du = lq / avg, sm = 1 / (0.4 + 0.6 * du);
      const base = v.need / rate * 60, adj = base * sm, days = +v.days, per = adj / days;
      const grade = du >= 0.7 ? ['good', 'Good'] : du >= 0.55 ? ['warn', 'Fair'] : ['bad', 'Poor'];
      let h = U.big('Run this zone', `${HM.fmt(Math.ceil(per), 0)} min`, `${days} day${days > 1 ? 's' : ''} a week, ${HM.fmt(Math.ceil(adj), 0)} minutes in total.`);
      h += U.kv([
        ['Application rate', U.f(rate, 'rate', 2)],
        ['Evenness (lower-quarter DU)', `${HM.fmt(du * 100, 0)}% <span class="tag ${grade[0]}">${grade[1]}</span>`],
        ['Water per watering day', U.f(v.need / days, 'wdep', 2)]
      ]);
      if (du < 0.55) h += U.note('Coverage is uneven. Before adding minutes, look for tilted, sunken, blocked or mismatched heads and fix those: it saves more water than any schedule.', 'bad');
      else if (du < 0.7) h += U.note('Coverage is fair. Straightening heads and clearing grass from around them usually improves it.');
      if (rate > 0.75 * 25.4) h += U.note(`This zone applies water quickly. On clay or slopes it will run off before it soaks in: use the <a href="cycle-and-soak.qmd?pr=${HM.fmt(rate, 2)}">cycle-and-soak scheduler</a> to split it into shorter cycles.`);
      else h += U.note(`Check for runoff on clay or slopes with the <a href="cycle-and-soak.qmd?pr=${HM.fmt(rate, 2)}">cycle-and-soak scheduler</a>.`, 'good');
      return {
        html: h, work: [
          `Average catch = ${U.f(avg, 'wdep', 3)} in ${HM.fmt(v.min, 1)} min (${n} cups)`,
          `Application rate = ${U.f(avg, 'wdep', 3)} ÷ ${HM.fmt(v.min / 60, 3)} hr = ${U.f(rate, 'rate', 2)}`,
          `Lowest quarter (${q} cup${q > 1 ? 's' : ''}) average = ${U.f(lq, 'wdep', 3)}; evenness DU = ${U.f(lq, 'wdep', 3)} ÷ ${U.f(avg, 'wdep', 3)} = ${HM.fmt(du, 2)}`,
          `Base run time = ${U.f(v.need, 'wdep', 2)} ÷ ${U.f(rate, 'rate', 2)} × 60 = ${HM.fmt(base, 1)} min per week`,
          `Scheduling multiplier = 1 ÷ (0.4 + 0.6 × ${HM.fmt(du, 2)}) = ${HM.fmt(sm, 2)}, so the drier spots get enough: ${HM.fmt(base, 1)} × ${HM.fmt(sm, 2)} = ${HM.fmt(adj, 1)} min per week`,
          `Per day = ${HM.fmt(adj, 1)} ÷ ${days} = ${HM.fmt(per, 1)} → ${Math.ceil(per)} min`
        ]
      };
    }
  });
})();
</script>

## What the numbers mean

- **Application rate** is how fast the zone puts water down. Spray heads are usually fast (1–2 in/hr); rotors and rotary nozzles are slow (0.3–0.7 in/hr). Zones with different head types need different run times.
- **Evenness (DU)** compares the driest quarter of the cups with the average. At 70% or above, coverage is good. Below about 55%, some spots get less than half as much as others, and adding minutes just floods the wet spots to rescue the dry ones.
- **Scheduling multiplier.** Because coverage is never perfect, the run time is stretched a little so the drier areas still get enough. Better coverage means a smaller multiplier and less water.

Repeat the test for each zone: zones rarely match. Once you know a zone's rate, the [cycle-and-soak scheduler](cycle-and-soak.qmd) checks whether your soil can absorb it that fast.

## References

Lower-quarter distribution uniformity and scheduling multiplier: Irrigation Association (2005). *Landscape Irrigation Scheduling and Water Management*. Irrigation Association, Falls Church, VA.
